title: 1992 AHSME Problem 20
statement: Part of an “\(n\)-pointed regular star” is shown. It is a simple closed polygon in which all \(2n\) edges are congruent, angles \(A_1,\) \(A_2,\) \(\ldots,\) \(A_n\) are congruent, and angles \(B_1,\) \(B_2,\) \(\ldots,\) \(B_n\) are congruent. If the acute angle at \(A_1\) is \(10^\circ\) less than the acute angle at \(B_1,\) then \(n=\)

solutions.text:
Let the acute angles at the tips and notches be \(\alpha\) and \(\beta,\) respectively, so \(\beta-\alpha=10^\circ.\) The \(2n\)-gon has \(n\) interior angles \(\alpha\) and \(n\) reflex interior angles \(360^\circ-\beta.\) Therefore \[ \begin{gathered} n\alpha+n(360^\circ-\beta)\\ {}=(2n-2)180^\circ. \end{gathered} \] Substituting \(\beta-\alpha=10^\circ\) gives \(350n=360n-360,\) so \(n=36.\)

Thus the correct answer is D.
hints: Let the acute angles at the \(A\)- and \(B\)-vertices be \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\)
